title: Sell Mineral Rights in Holloway, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Holloway, OH
metaDescription: Holloway sits in Belmont County, in one of Ohio's most active Utica/Point Pleasant drilling corridors. See what that means for your mineral rights.
heroLead: Holloway sits in a part of Belmont County where coal mining gave way to shale drilling almost smoothly, and mineral title here often reflects both eras.
intro: Holloway is a small village in Belmont County, one of the most heavily drilled counties in the Utica/Point Pleasant play, in an area whose economy ran on coal mining for most of the 20th century before horizontal drilling arrived. Mineral ownership around Holloway frequently traces back to coal-company land transactions from decades ago, often involving severances that separated coal from oil and gas rights entirely.

sections.heading: From coal camp to shale corridor
paragraphs: Holloway's history as a coal community means a lot of the surrounding land passed through mining-company ownership before returning to farm families or being sold outright, and each of those transactions could have affected how minerals were reserved. Belmont County's subsequent Utica development means many of these same tracts are now inside active spacing units, so real production data often exists for the area even where a specific parcel's history is complicated.

sections.heading: Untangling coal-era paperwork before pricing your interest
paragraphs: Because coal and oil and gas were frequently severed separately here, confirming exactly what your family's mineral reservation covers requires reading the actual recorded deed at the Belmont County Recorder's office in St. Clairsville rather than assuming based on what a neighboring parcel's history looks like. Once that's confirmed, checking for any lease or unitization order tied to your specific tract completes the picture.

faqs.question: Did coal mining in Holloway affect oil and gas mineral rights?
faqs.answer: It can have, since coal was often severed separately from oil and gas in this area, sometimes to entirely different parties. The original severance deed will clarify what was actually reserved and by whom.

faqs.question: Is Holloway in an actively producing part of Belmont County?
faqs.answer: Belmont County has seen extensive Utica/Point Pleasant development, and many tracts in this area sit inside producing units, though it varies parcel to parcel.

faqs.question: How do I confirm whether my interest is tied to a currently producing well?
faqs.answer: Check for recent royalty statements, or search the Belmont County Recorder's records for any lease and unitization order recorded against your parcel.

faqs.question: What documents help establish my exact interest before selling?
faqs.answer: Your deed or severance instrument, any lease or division order, and recent royalty statements if you receive them, which together establish your net mineral acres and decimal interest.
